raw_response:
I've been farming these 12 mu for 40 years, since I was 19. My father taught me everything, and I mostly do what he did, with some small changes I've picked up from watching my neighbors and from my own hard lessons.

My wheat went in last October, around the 10th, same as always. I buy improved seed from the agricultural shop in town — costs me about 40 yuan per mu. I don't save my own wheat seed, it's too much trouble and the shop seed grows better. Before planting I put down base fertilizer, about one big bag of that three-in-one compound stuff for every two mu. Then at this time of year, when the wheat is standing up tall and green, I topdress with about half a bag of urea per mu. My neighbor Li uses a bit more, but last year I got about 900 jin per mu and that's fine for me — not great, not bad, enough to get by. I irrigate three times for wheat: once after planting if the autumn is dry, once now at this growing time, and once when the wheat is heading and filling grain. Water from the well costs electricity money, so I don't waste it, but three times is what I've always done and it works unless the winter is very dry.

In June I'll hire a combine harvester to cut the wheat — 50 yuan per mu but it's fast, and I need to get the maize in quick. That window between wheat coming off and maize going in is only about a week, sometimes less if it rains and the ground gets muddy. I plant hybrid maize seed, about 60 yuan per mu. For maize I do similar fertilizer: compound at planting, then urea when the plants are about knee-high. Two irrigations for maize, three if July is very dry and the leaves start curling. I spray herbicide for both crops — weeds are my biggest headache, worse than bugs. I don't bother with insecticide much unless I see a real problem.

There are six of us in the house, but my son and older daughter work off-farm in the city now, so it's mainly me, my wife, and my younger daughter doing the farm work. I hire a few days of help at harvest and planting time — 100 to 120 yuan per day now, which hurts, but we can't manage the rush by ourselves, especially getting the maize in before the window closes.

All the seed, fertilizer, water, pesticides, and hired labor comes to about 5,800 yuan for the year. That's a lot of money for our family. Sometimes I think about using less fertilizer to save a few hundred yuan, but then I remember the year I tried that — maybe 2015 — and the yield dropped badly. I lost more from the bad harvest than I would have saved on fertilizer. Now I play it safe — I'd rather spend a bit more and make sure we have enough grain and some income. If the weather is normal, I expect about 900 jin per mu of wheat and about 1,000 jin per mu of maize.
